Bonus · when things break

Damage & AirCover

What to do when something big goes wrong, and how to get your money back.

Bonus★

A flood, a broken pipe, a smashed TV. Sooner or later something big happens. Your job is to fix the problem. Airbnb’s job is to look after the guests and help pay for the damage. That is what the fees are for.

The first 24 hours

1

Stop the damage

Make it safe first: turn off the water or power and call an emergency professional.

2

Tell your guests

Fast, honest and short: what happened, what you are doing, when you’ll update them.

3

Document everything

Photos and videos of the damage, the dates, every message, every invoice.

4

Call Airbnb support

Open a case early. Is the place no longer livable? Airbnb takes care of the guests.

5

Fix it with professionals

Get it repaired properly, and ask for itemized invoices with dates.

Let the guest stop the damage

Water pouring from a pipe at 2am? Sparks from a socket? You can’t always get there fast, but your guest is already there. If you know exactly where the main valves and switches are, with photos, you can guide them in one message and stop the problem in minutes, without waiting for you or a technician.

Main water valve

Where it is, with a photo. Turn it off and the leak stops.

Gas valve

Close it if there is a gas smell, open the windows and call the emergency number.

Electrical panel

Which switch is the main one. Flip it down if there are sparks or a burning smell.

Example

The leak at night

Guest

Help! Water is coming out of the pipe under the sink, the floor is flooding!

You

Thanks for telling us so fast! Please close the main water valve: it’s in the cupboard next to the washing machine, the red handle (photo attached). Turn it to the right until it stops. Our plumber is on the way.

Why it works One message, a photo, and the damage stops in two minutes instead of two hours.

Even with one property, write it down once. With several, it’s essential: you won’t remember where every valve is. Our property manual has a place for all of it.

Open your property manual

Not your job: hotels for your guests

If your place becomes unlivable, you don’t have to book or pay hotels for your guests. Airbnb’s Rebooking and Refund Policy covers it: Airbnb gives the guest a full or partial refund, or helps them find a similar place. Focus on fixing the problem.

Be ready for one thing: the refund for the nights that were affected is taken from your payout. Agree on it with Airbnb and your guests, and move on.
Airbnb’s Rebooking and Refund Policy

How AirCover for Hosts works

AirCover is Airbnb’s protection for hosts. Its Host damage protection reimburses you up to $3 million USD when guests damage your place or belongings and don’t pay for it.

Covered

  • Damage to your home, furniture and belongings caused by guests
  • Extra cleaning, like stains, pet accidents or smoke smell
  • Income lost if you must cancel bookings because of guest damage

Not covered

  • Normal wear and tear
  • Acts of nature, like earthquakes or storms
  • Lost cash, and anything booked outside Airbnb
AirCover for Hosts

How to claim, step by step

1

Document the damage

Photos, videos, repair quotes and receipts.

2

Request the money from the guest

Within 14 days of the guest’s checkout, go to the Resolution Center and click “Request money”.

3

Wait 24 hours

The guest has 24 hours to pay, pay part of it or decline.

4

Click “Involve Airbnb”

No payment? Airbnb support reviews your request and pays from AirCover.

5

Get paid

Once it’s approved, the payout usually arrives in 3 to 7 business days.

Invoices win claims. Ask every professional for an itemized invoice with the date, the address and what was done. Add before and after photos, and keep every message on Airbnb.

Your Resolution Center

All your requests are in one place: airbnb.com/resolutions. There you see who paid and who didn’t. When a guest doesn’t respond, the “Involve Airbnb” button appears: click it, and Airbnb pays from AirCover.

Open the Resolution Center

Real case: the blocked sewage pipe

The biggest problem we ever had

A five-bedroom apartment in Barcelona, five separate bookings. The building’s main sewage pipe got blocked. Every time the neighbors upstairs flushed, water and sewage came up through our showers and flooded the bathrooms.

5bookings affected
4–5days to fix it
€2,500spent in total
~95%reimbursed by Airbnb

How we solved it

  1. We called a 24-hour drain company. The pipe was so blocked that the technicians had to abseil down the outside of the building to reach it.
  2. We booked our cleaner for extra days, so the apartment stayed as clean and pleasant as possible.
  3. We kept the guests updated and agreed refunds for the affected nights with Airbnb. We didn’t book hotels: that is Airbnb’s part.
  4. We uploaded every invoice with photos to the Resolution Center. Airbnb reimbursed around 95% of what we spent.
This is what the fees are for

Stay calm, fix the problem, document everything, and let Airbnb do its part. Without AirCover, this week would have cost us €2,500. With it, almost nothing.

Bonus · learn from ours

Common mistakes

The mistakes we see hosts make most, and how to avoid them.

Bonus★

Whether you’re just getting started or already managing several listings, these are the pitfalls that cost hosts the most time, money and peace of mind. We made most of them ourselves, so you don’t have to.

Guests & bookings

✕

Unclear late-night check-ins

Guests arriving after midnight run into more problems. Make your self-check-in foolproof, or expect urgent calls at 2am.

Self-check-in, Lesson 12 →
✕

Accepting “change” requests to dodge fees

Some guests ask to shorten their stay only to avoid the cancellation fee. Decline and stick to your policy. It protects your income.

✕

Bookings outside the platform

Saving on fees is tempting, but it removes all protection for you and the guest. Keep messages and payments on the platform.

✕

Taking it personally

Most guests are amazing, but once in a while one is simply unfair. Stay calm, stay professional and stick to the facts.

Difficult guests, Bonus lesson →Handling complaints, Lesson 9 →

Your team & money

✕

No photos from your cleaner

If something is damaged or missing (even towels), photos are your evidence for claims and disputes. Make it part of every turnover.

Damage & AirCover, Bonus lesson →
✕

Expecting the perfect hire first time

Most people won’t be a perfect fit on the first try. Don’t be afraid to change until your team is reliable.

Build your team, Lesson 10 →
✕

One person doing everything

Split communication, finances and maintenance, so nothing falls apart when someone is unavailable.

✕

Sharing all your numbers

Not everyone on your team needs to see your earnings. Too much information can create tension or unrealistic expectations.

In the property

✕

No spare key or backup access

Keys get lost or stolen. Without a plan B you risk lockouts, unhappy guests and expensive emergency locksmiths.

✕

Unlabeled washing machine

Put a clear sticker or arrow on the right program. Otherwise guests pick the 3-hour cycle, which costs you more and blocks the machine.

✕

Long messages and labels

Travelers are tired and skip long texts. Keep scheduled messages and labels short and to the point.

✕

Fragile wine glasses

They always break. Keep extras in stock, or switch to more durable ones.

✕

Bulky storage

Store duvets and other bulky items in vacuum bags. They take less space and stay clean.

The takeaway

Avoid these, and your hosting gets smoother, safer and more professional. Most of them take five minutes to fix today.

Legal & local rules

AI prompt: discover the local rental rules in your area
Can you help me find the current rules for renting out a property in ? I want to understand the rules for short-term rentals (under 1 month), mid-term rentals (1 to 6 months) and long-term rentals, and for subletting a property I rent (rental arbitrage). For each type of rental, I want to know: - If it is legal, and under which conditions - Whether I need a license, permit or registration - Any minimum or maximum stay rules, or limits on the number of nights per year - Tax obligations (income tax, tourist or occupancy tax) - Zoning restrictions, primary residence rules or building/HOA rules - What a landlord needs to agree to if I want to sublet - Whether I can do this as a private individual, or need to register as self-employed or a company Please include any helpful links or resources to official government sites if available. At the end, add a short summary I can copy into my notes, in this format: - Short-term rentals (under 1 month): allowed / not allowed / with conditions - Mid-term rentals (1–6 months): allowed / not allowed / with conditions - Long-term rentals: allowed / not allowed / with conditions - Subletting (rental arbitrage): allowed / not allowed / with conditions - License or permit needed: yes / no (and which one) - Minimum stay: ... - Taxes: ... - Other important rules: ...

Nightly prices for similar listings (low, typical, high) in high and low season 2. Occupancy by month, and which months are high and low season 3. Copy and open in:ChatGPTGeminiClaude

Pitch landlords

Cold email to a landlord
Subject: Your rental property Hi , I saw your property and I'm interested in renting it. I run a small property management company, and I'd love to tell you more about how we work. Would you be open to a quick call or meeting this week? Best regards,
Face-to-face pitch framework
Start with rapport: "Thanks for taking the time to meet. I'd like to explain a rental arrangement that could work well for both of us." Position the offer: "I run a small property rental business. I rent properties and host for stays. All our guests are ID-verified." Why it's easier than a normal tenant: "You get guaranteed payment: the rent is on time, every month. We work with a professional cleaner and handyman, so the place is always kept in excellent condition. No late payments, no chasing tenants, and no hidden damage at the end of a contract." Good communication: "You'll have one point of contact: me. I'll keep you updated and I'm always easy to reach." Close confidently: "Would you be open to giving this a try? We can put everything in a clear written agreement."
Follow-up email after a conversation
Subject: Follow-up on our conversation Hi , Thanks again for taking the time to chat. I know this approach may be different from a standard long-term rental, so I'd like to highlight the key benefits for you, especially compared with the typical risks landlords face. With a standard rental, it's common to experience things like: - Tenants who don't pay rent on time or stop paying altogether - Properties left in poor condition after move-out - Difficulties accessing the property for inspections or maintenance - Disputes over damage, deposits or responsibility for upkeep What we offer is a hands-off, professional arrangement that protects your property and gives you peace of mind: Monthly rent: , guaranteed and on time, every month Guests: ID-verified Cleaning: Professionally cleaned, far more often than with a standard tenant Maintenance: Regularly inspected and maintained by our professional handyman, at no cost to you I'll attach our information brochure about rental arbitrage, so you can see exactly how it works. Let me know if you have any questions. I'm happy to explain anything in more detail. Looking forward to hearing your thoughts,
